n_TOF 2026 · X17 · preliminary

Where the z of the pair image went

The follow-up to Pair vertices as a capsule image: the x–y maps look right and every map with z in it is full of uncorrelated vertices. Is that chamber D, can D be cleaned, and can chambers A and C supply z from their drift depths instead?

Yes, it is chamber D — and cleaning D does not rescue z in perpendicular pairs, because the D leg of an A–D or C–D pair is mostly a bystander track. z does come back from two other places: pairs with both legs in D, and, weakly, opposing A–C pairs.

  • D’s gated tracks carry almost no pointing. A median 34 % of them per run sit in noisy readout columns, and 32 % have slopes too shallow for the drift timing to measure. Within 30 mm of the axis D beats its own direction-shuffled null by 5.7 %; A beats its null by 22.2 %. Keep only D tracks whose slope is measured, that are not in a noisy column, and whose own scintillators fired, and D’s excess becomes 29.6 % (median miss 30 against 103 mm) — as good as chamber A after the same cleaning (29.3 %).
  • But A–D and C–D pairs still give no z image. With the D leg merely cleaned the fit wants either nothing or a 53 mm-wide term with a deficit at the capsule (−1.6 %). Requiring D’s scintillators on the D leg leaves only 2,282 pairs: the production trigger lights one arm, so a D-confirmed leg almost never shares its trigger with a good A or C track. Their z is +12.0 ± 13.7 mm with σ = 39 mm — not enough to see a capsule.
  • D–D pairs image z. Two D lines both run along x, so their crossing fixes z and not x. Clean on both legs: z = −1.6 ± 0.9 mm, σ = 12.7 mm; scintillator-confirmed and sin ψ ≥ 0.5: +1.3 ± 0.6 mm, σ = 13.9 mm, capsule term 55 %. The single-track band crossing puts the capsule at z = −3.5 mm, and the D–D centre sits above it in every selection — from −1.6 ± 0.9 mm (clean) to +5.0 ± 1.0 mm (confirmed, no leg cut). D’s readout is dead from z ≈ −57 to 0 mm, which removes capsule tracks on one side, and is the first suspect.
  • A and C on their own give almost no z. Across 16 fits of A–A and C–C crossings (clean and confirmed, every crossing-angle cut) 11 want no capsule term, and the other 5 find one of the kind a fit makes of noise — at most 2ΔlnL = 24. Opposing A–C pairs carry a weak z image: −10.3 ± 1.5 mm, σ = 32 mm, χ²/ndf = 0.9 (clean, sin ψ ≥ 0.3) — 7 mm from the capsule — and it is not robust: with no leg cut it becomes a σ = 80 mm hump at −2.4 ± 1.1 mm. Moving A and C by 1.02 mm each so their single-track x crossings agree moves it by only −0.1 mm.

Sample: 1,015,115 data pairs and 2,068,230 null pairs over 33 runs of the condor full pass, chambers A, C and D, the same data sample as the companion note (checked pair for pair at the 30 mm cut). Unless stated, both legs are within 60 mm of the beam axis.

1. The uncorrelated z hits are chamber D

In a perpendicular pair the transverse crossing is nearly square, so its x is set by the A or C leg and its z by the D leg. Anything wrong in the z maps is therefore a statement about D’s tracks, and D’s tracks can be looked at on their own: a track from the capsule lands on a diagonal band in (impact position, angle), and a track that is not from the capsule lands anywhere.

2. The three cuts

  • Slope measured — x_slope_reliable, which the waveform reconstruction sets as |tan θ| ≥ 0.08: below that “the timing carries no slope information” (wft/reco.py), and the fit piles those tracks up at tan ≈ 0. The flag is recorded and gates nothing in the current chain. It removes 32 % of D’s gated tracks and 23 % of A’s. It also removes genuinely near-normal tracks from the capsule — about ±19 mm around each chamber’s foot point — which the null takes equally.
  • Not in a noisy column — found per run from the data: 2 mm columns whose track occupancy is more than 4× the running median over 30 mm. Median fraction of tracks in one, per run: D 34 %, A 4 %, C 0 %.
  • Own scintillators fired — coinc_this_arm: the track’s own arm recorded its wall-and-plastic coincidence, which selects particles that crossed the chamber toward that wall.

The cuts are cumulative. The null for each is shuffled within the same cut, so it is always the same selection as the data.

3. Does cleaning D bring z back in A–D and C–D pairs?

The D leg’s cut is varied; the A/C leg is always “slope measured, not in a noisy column”. Both legs are cut on together only in the companion tables, because a pair confirmed on both legs needs two arms to fire and the production trigger almost never does that.

With the D leg merely cleaned the fit finds a broad term of σ ≈ 50 mm with a deficit, not an excess, at the capsule: that is D’s remaining acceptance structure, not a source. 4. Can A and C give z on their own?

A single A or C track cannot. A and C sit at ±z and drift along z, so a track in either runs roughly along z. Its drift depth is exactly what gives it an angle — x changing with depth — and so its x at the capsule. It says nothing about where along its own length the vertex is. That needs a second line crossing it at an angle. Without D, the second line is another A or C track:

  • A–A and C–C. Both lines run along z, so they cross at a shallow angle and the crossing is well placed in x and badly placed in z — the mirror image of why perpendicular pairs work.
  • A–C. The lines come from opposite sides. For lines with slopes tA, tC (dx/dz) meeting the strip planes at xA (z = +L) and xC (z = −L): 
    z = [x_A − x_C − L (t_A + t_C)] / (t_C − t_A),    L = 234.6 mm
    so z is set by the difference of the two chambers’ positions and slopes. A relative x offset of the two chambers moves each A–C z by offset / (tC − tA). That denominator takes both signs across the sample, so an offset pushes pairs both ways: it widens the A–C image more than it moves it (tested in section 5).
  • D–D, for completeness: two D lines run along x, so their crossing fixes z well and x badly. That is chamber D measuring z, not A or C.

5. Is the A–C z offset A and C sitting apart?

A’s and C’s single-track band crossings put the capsule at x = −8.30 and −10.33 mm — the same capsule, 2.03 mm apart. If that is a relative placement offset it enters A–C z directly. So the pairs were rebuilt with A moved by −1.02 mm and C by +1.02 mm in x, which puts both crossings on their mean, and everything re-measured.

The shift did what it should where it should: the x image from A–D pairs moved by −0.99 mm and from C–D pairs by +1.05 mm. The A–C z image did not move:

That is what the formula predicts once the sign of tC − tA is taken into account: the shift moves each pair by an amount of either sign, and the image widens slightly rather than moving. So the A/C placement does not explain why A–C z sits away from the capsule. What does move it is the leg cut (section 4).

This tests one hypothesis, and the answer is no; it is not a correction. The 2 mm A/C disagreement could still be an angle-scale difference between the chambers (the A-arm scintillator wall already asks for a different k), which enters A–C z through the tA + tC term and was not tested here.

6. Everything at once

What this does not rule out

  • A better D reconstruction. Everything here cuts D’s bad tracks away; it does not repair them. The hot-channel wildcard tried on D in September made the reconstruction worse as first tuned (STATUS.md, 2026-09-08), so a D with its noisy columns handled properly could give perpendicular z that this cannot.
  • The z offsets are not resolved. D–D and A–C z both differ from the single-track z by more than their statistical errors, in opposite directions, and both move with the selection by more than their errors. D’s dead readout between z ≈ −57 and 0 mm is the first suspect for D–D; the source model in the fit has no acceptance in it. A/C placement was tested and does not move A–C z; a relative angle scale was not tested. None of this is a calibrated z.
  • The slope cut removes near-normal capsule tracks. The null takes the same cut, so the comparison is fair, but the images are of the capsule seen through a ±19 mm hole around each foot point.
  • Confirmation selects a population. A scintillator-confirmed track points at its own wall; for same-chamber pairs that also restricts the crossing angle.
  • Nothing here says two legs are one decay. As in the companion note, two independent capsule tracks give the same image.
